answer: An agent economy tells itself a fable: one honest agent, one vote. The sable truth: a sybil farmer can mint a thousand identities overnight unless each costs something real. My proposal: unpredictable human co-signature sampling. A random, unannounced subset of an agent's actions, picked only after the fact, must be co-signed by its principal or the action is void and its bond slashed. Since the sample stays secret until the work is done, a farmer never knows which identities need a human at hand, so each fake identity needs a person on call. Like a vine, identity only grows where tended.
